claims.claim: SemiLEDs’ core business is the development, manufacture and sale of LED chips, components, modules and sensor systems for general lighting and specialty industrial applications.
claims.quote: We develop, manufacture and sell light emitting diode (LED) chips and LED components, LED modules, sensor components incorporating LED or VCSEL and systems. Our products are used for general lighting and specialty industrial applications, including ultraviolet, or UV, curing of polymers, LED light therapy in medical/cosmetic applications, counterfeit detection, germicidal and virucidal devices, LED lighting for horticulture applications, architectural lighting and entertainment lighting and sensing of pressure or distance using LED or VCSEL. In addition, in fiscal years 2026 and 2025, we entered into a number of buy-sell orders for equipment that we purchased and then sold to our customers.

claims.claim: The company packages its LED chips into components for distributors and end‑customers in selected markets including Taiwan, Europe, Japan and the United States.
claims.quote: We package our LED chips into LED components or sensor components, which we sell to distributors and a customer base in a few select markets, including Taiwan, Europe, Japan and the United States. We also sell our “Enhanced Vertical,” or EV, LED product series in blue, white, green and UV in selected markets. We sell our LED chips to packagers or to distributors, who in turn sell to packagers.

claims.claim: SemiLEDs has adopted a fabless business model, using foundry fabs to ODM its chips and seeking to sell idle chip‑manufacturing equipment to lower capacity costs.
claims.quote: We have moved to a fabless business model in which we utilize foundry fabs to ODM our chips using our developed technology and continue to explore opportunities to sell our chip manufacturing equipment, which will help us to reduce the idle capacity costs.

claims.claim: The firm concentrates on high‑value UV LED applications after exiting the highly price‑compressed general lighting market.
claims.quote: SemiLEDs had moved away from general lighting markets due to extreme price erosion led by companies in China. We have moved on to focus on industrial UV applications.

claims.claim: Revenue and gross margin performance in FY 2026 were driven largely by buy‑sell equipment orders, which represented 85% of total revenue for the year.
claims.quote: In fiscal years 2026 and 2025, the Company entered into a number of buy‑sell orders for equipment that it purchased and then sold to its customers, and the Company anticipates continuing to receive buy‑sell purchase orders in fiscal year 2027.

claims.claim: Buy‑sell equipment orders generated $16.0 million of revenue in FY 2026, substantially higher than the $10.2 million cost of revenue associated with those orders.
claims.quote: In fiscal years 2026 and 2025, the revenue relating to these purchase orders was $16.0 million and $40.6 million, and the associated cost of revenue was $10.2 million and $36.5 million, for fiscal years 2026 and 2025, respectively.

claims.claim: SemiLEDs’ top ten customers accounted for 96% of FY 2026 revenue, highlighting a highly concentrated customer base.
claims.quote: We have historically derived a significant portion of our revenues from a limited number of customers. For the years ended August 31, 2026 and 2025, our top ten customers collectively accounted for 96% and 99% of our revenues, respectively.

claims.claim: Management plans to increase resources toward module and system design to offer a one‑stop solution for UV industrial printers, horticulture lighting and disinfection markets.
claims.quote: To differentiate ourselves from other LED package manufacturers, we are putting more resources towards module and system design. Along with our technical know-how in the chip and package sectors, we are able to further integrate electrical, thermal and mechanical manufacturing resources to provide customers with one‑stop system services.

claims.claim: R&D focus is on design methodology, process technology, yield improvement and larger wafer sizes to reduce production costs.
claims.quote: We focus our research and development efforts on our design methodology and process technology for our LED products. We also focus on improving our production yields and increasing wafer sizes to lower our production costs.

claims.claim: Management acknowledges that rapid technical change and intense competition create pricing pressure that may erode gross margins.
claims.quote: Competition in the markets for LED products is intense, and we expect that competition will continue to increase, thereby creating a highly aggressive pricing environment. Some of our competitors have in the past reduced their average selling prices, and the resulting competitive pricing pressures have caused us to similarly reduce our prices, accelerating the decline in the gross margin of our products.

claims.claim: The company’s strategy includes cost‑reduction measures such as disposing idle equipment and lowering capital expenditures, but further workforce reductions could pose legal and talent‑retention risks.
claims.quote: In addition, we have implemented certain actions to accelerate operating cost reductions and improve operational efficiencies… We also disposed of a certain level of our idle equipment to reduce the excess capacity charges that we have suffered for many years.

claims.claim: Judgment: Pursuing additional buy‑sell equipment orders in FY 2027 could stabilize cash flow, but reliance on this segment creates revenue volatility if order volume drops.
claims.quote: We anticipate continuing to receive buy‑sell purchase orders in fiscal year 2027. As a result of these purchase orders and associated uncertainty of the business, our revenue, cost of revenues, receivables, inventories and customer deposits over future quarters may vary significantly.

gaps: The 10‑K does not provide quantitative forecasts for FY 2027 revenue or margin trends, so any specific growth outlook beyond FY 2026 cannot be sourced.
There is no disclosed timeline or budget for the planned expansion of module‑system design resources, so the magnitude of this initiative cannot be quantified.
